consistency.detail: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, not CC BY as the shortlist assumed: property values withheld.
Table 1 is titled 'Eccentricity based topological indices' but every formula uses M_u, which is not defined; the worked example uses neighborhood-degree-like edge partitions.
Oxcarbazepine (A12) and eslicarbazepine (A14) have identical index rows, as expected for the same hydrogen-suppressed graph; their properties differ.
Both blocks of Table 9 are labelled 'Metrics for Traditional Artificial Neural Network'; the second is presumably the fuzzy ANN.

resolution_issues: Lacosamide is listed twice (A10 and A18); both resolve to CID 219078 and have identical rows in Tables 3 and 5. Effective n = 19.
The Methods repeat the drug list without zonisamide (19 names, lacosamide twice).

reasons: ANN/FANN architecture (layers, units, epochs actually used, seeds) and the evaluation protocol for Table 9 are not specified
the index family is ambiguous (M_u undefined; titled eccentricity based)
lacosamide appears twice (A10, A18) and zonisamide is missing from the second drug list, so the effective n is 19
the drug list and ChemSpider property values could still feed the size-baseline and CV chain of Experiment D
